record.paper_title: Open problems in billiards and quantitative symplectic geometry
record.original_question: Describe the dynamics, at least for generic trajectories, of parallelogram tiling billiards: the planar tiling by parallelograms with side vectors a = (a,0) and b = (b sin alpha, b cos alpha), where a and b are positive and alpha lies between 0 and pi, as the parameters alpha and m = a/b vary.

evidence.quote: The question is to describe the dynamics

artifact.self_contained_problem: Consider the planar tiling by congruent parallelograms whose sides are given by the vectors $\mathbf{a}=(a,0)$ and $\mathbf{b}=(b\sin\alpha, b\cos\alpha)$, where $a>0$, $b>0$, and $\alpha\in(0,\pi)$. A "tiling billiard" trajectory in this tiling is a piecewise linear oriented curve in the plane that travels in straight lines inside each parallelogram tile and, upon crossing an edge of the tiling, refracts so that the outgoing direction is the reflection of the incoming direction across the edge (i.e., the angle of incidence equals the angle of refraction on the opposite side of the edge, corresponding to refraction with coefficient $-1$). Let $m=a/b$. Describe the dynamics of such trajectories, at least for almost every initial condition (generic trajectories), as the parameters $\alpha\in(0,\pi)$ and $m\in(0,\infty)$ vary: classify possible behaviors (periodic, drift-periodic, escaping, dense, etc.) and how they depend on $(\alpha,m)$.
artifact.status_search_result: Tiling billiards in various tilings (triangle, trihexagonal, cyclic polygons) have been actively studied since their introduction by Davis et al. (2018), with recent results on triangle tilings, cyclic polygon tilings, and wind-tree tiling billiards (2024–2026). However, no general classification of dynamics for the two-parameter family of parallelogram tiling billiards (in terms of $\alpha$ and $m=a/b$) appears in the literature; the question remains open.

status_evidence.title: Deviations for Generalized Tiling Billiards in Cyclic Polygons
status_evidence.snippet: Tiling billiards is a class of dynamical system introduced by Davis et al. in 2018. ... There exist examples with periodic, drift-periodic or linearly escaping trajectories.
status_evidence.claim: Tiling billiards dynamics depend strongly on the tiling; classifications exist only for specific cases (triangles, cyclic polygons, trihexagonal), not parallelograms generally.

status_evidence.title: Wind-tree tiling billiards and their trapping strips
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work (2026) on related tiling-billiards models indicates active research with no full classification for parallelogram tilings.
status_evidence.claim: The dynamics for parallelogram tiling billiards as $(\alpha,m)$ vary has not been classified.
